{"id": "60f1ee3e-c4a7-4292-b842-726399a8c28a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I can only partly answer this. The documentation I checked doesn't define "AWS-6", and you haven't given me the vpc-cni version, so I can't name CVEs.

**CIS 5.1.1**
- From memory of the CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark, 5.1.1 is "Ensure Image Vulnerability Scanning using Amazon ECR image scanning or a third party provider". The documentation I found confirms the CIS EKS Benchmark exists but doesn't quote this control's text.
- If that wording is right, the control checks that scanning is configured, not how many findings come back. With Inspector enhanced ECR scanning enabled, it should report **PASS**.
- The zero CRITICAL/HIGH findings is supporting evidence. It shouldn't change the result.
- The vpc-cni version lag has no bearing on 5.1.1. Treat that as a separate item.
- Some tools add their own conditions, such as requiring scan-on-push or coverage of every repository. Check your tool's definition of the control to be sure.

**Supplementary check AWS-6**
- "AWS-6" isn't a CIS control, and I found no AWS documentation for it. It's probably specific to the compliance tool or ruleset you're using.
- Because of that, I can't say what it reports. It plausibly covers add-on version currency, which would make a two-minor-versions-behind vpc-cni a WARN or FAIL. That is a guess.
- If you paste the check's definition or output, I can interpret it.

**CVEs for the vpc-cni version**
- "Two minor versions behind" doesn't identify a release, so I can't map it to specific CVEs. I also won't guess CVE IDs.
- Inspector's zero CRITICAL/HIGH result covers the images it scanned. That should include the `amazon-k8s-cni` image if it's in ECR and in scope. It doesn't prove the version is free of CVEs. Inspector may not have covered it, for example if the image is pulled from an AWS-managed ECR repo outside your account's scan configuration. Lower-severity findings also wouldn't show up in your count.
- To get a definitive answer, send me the exact add-on version, such as `v1.xx.x-eksbuild.n`. I can then check the AWS documentation and security bulletins for it. You can also look the image up in Inspector by its tag.

Which compliance tool or ruleset defines AWS-6, and what is the vpc-cni version?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
